name: mimalloc aligned-hint allocation inside the 2TiB-30TiB reserved hint area
required_postconditions: the host provides at least 46 bits of usable virtual address space, otherwise the whole hinting strategy is disabled at os.c:119
the [2TiB, 30TiB) window is habitually free, so a hint aimed into it is usually honoured and the returned address is usually already MI_SEGMENT_ALIGN aligned
if the hint is not honoured the result is only slower, never wrong: unix_mmap_prim_aligned falls through to a plain mmap and the over-allocate-and-trim path fixes the alignment

location.symbol: unix_mmap_prim_aligned: fall back to regular mmap

failure_sink.description: if the hinted mmap returns something that is not aligned to try_alignment, prim.c logs _mi_trace_message("unable to directly request hinted aligned OS memory ...") and still returns the pointer; if it returned MAP_FAILED the function retries once without the hint. Exactly one retry, then the generic aligned path takes over. Nothing here is fatal.

source_locations.symbol: #define MI_HINT_MAX  ((uintptr_t)30 << 40) // wrap after 30TiB (area after 32TiB is used for huge OS pages)
if (mi_os_mem_config.virtual_address_bits < 46) return NULL;  // < 64TiB virtual address space
if (hint%try_alignment != 0) return NULL; - mimalloc refuses to emit a hint it knows is misaligned
p = unix_mmap_prim(hint, size, protect_flags, flags, fd); - plain mmap, hint only

extraction_limitations: the actual hint is a running atomic counter seeded at MI_HINT_BASE (os.c:126-136); 0x20000000000 is the seed value, not a fixed address the program will always use
the 46-bit virtual-address-space precondition at os.c:119 has no field in this schema; it is carried only as a postcondition string

x_campaign.rationale: 0x20000000000 is 32MiB-aligned so the declared-alignment branch of rule_address_alignment passes, exact placement is not required and relocation is permitted, and the probe observed 0x20000000000-0x20000400000 as available so the hint branch of rule_range_availability should not fire either.
